extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS 2020 reviewers (and area chairs / program committee members)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewing NeurIPS 2020 submissions: responsibilities, confidentiality, review content and scoring, discussion/author-response behavior, and administrative/formatting policies for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities (assignment & duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reviewer will be assigned around 4-6 submissions and is responsible for reviewing submissions, reading author responses, discussing submissions and author responses with other reviewers and area chairs (ACs), and helping make decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing process is double blind at reviewer/AC level; reviews and meta-reviews will be made public after decisions (identities remain anonymous). As soon as assigned, log into CMT to check conflicts and area-fit; if not comfortable, fill out a note in CMT and notify AC immediately so an alternate can be found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Please respect deadlines and respond to emails as promptly as possible!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most emails come from CMT (email@msr-cmt.org) and may be marked as spam—check spam and whitelist. If changing email address, update CMT. Keep domain conflicts up to date to prevent conflicts during review. If you will be unavailable for more than a few days, especially during important windows (e.g., discussion), inform your ACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must log in to CMT to check for conflicts and ensure papers fall within their expertise; read what constitutes conflict of interest for NeurIPS 2020.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uncomfortable reviewing, fill out a note in CMT and communicate to AC. DO NOT talk to other reviewers/ACs/SACs about submissions assigned to you without AC approval. DO NOT talk to others about your own submissions or submissions with which you have a conflict. Keep domain conflicts in CMT updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: You must keep everything relating to the review process confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions in your own work until they become publicly available. Do not talk about or distribute submissions (code, ideas, results) without program chairs' prior approval. Code submitted for review cannot be distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process is double blind at the level of reviewers and ACs (they cannot see author identities) but not at the level of SACs and program chairs. Authors are responsible for anonymizing submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission is not adequately anonymized (author names, affiliations, acknowledgements, or identifying information), contact the corresponding AC. Under no circumstances should you attempt to find out the authors' identities (e.g., via Google or arXiv); if you accidentally learn them, do not divulge them and do not let identities influence your decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit up to 100MB of supplementary material (proofs, derivations, data, source code); must be PDF or ZIP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your responsibility is to read and review the submission itself; examining supplementary material is discretionary. Since submissions are short, you may wish to look at supplementary material before criticizing a submission for insufficient details, proofs, or experimental results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executing submitted code & clicking links safely
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted code may contain security vulnerabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If running supplementary source code, do so in a secure environment: (1) inside a Docker container, (2) a VM image (VirtualBox/VMware), or (3) on a network-isolated cloud instance. Be cautious accessing web links provided from the paper as they may contain vulnerabilities or log visitor IP addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are limited to eight content pages, including all figures and tables, in the NeurIPS 'submission' style; additional pages containing only a) discussion of broader impact and b) references are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must use the NeurIPS 2020 LaTeX style file. If assigned submissions violate style (e.g., decreased margins or font size) or page limits, notify the AC immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions identical or substantially similar to papers in submission to, accepted to, or published in other archival venues (or to other NeurIPS submissions) should be deemed dual submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slicing contributions too thinly may be dual submission. If you suspect a submission is a dual submission or need clarification, contact the corresponding AC. See Call for Papers and FAQ for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content importance (quality of reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review content is the primary means by which ACs, SACs, and program chairs make decisions and is how authors understand decisions; make reviews detailed and informative; short, superficial reviews are worse than no review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews for rejected submissions should help authors improve; reviews for accepted papers should help with camera-ready versions. Provide clear, specific, and constructive feedback rather than uninformed opinions or guesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review submission mechanism (CMT usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviews must be submitted via the NeurIPS 2020 CMT site. You may revise reviews as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are both author and reviewer, use the same email for both roles. Never reply directly to CMT emails—use the 'email meta-reviewer' and 'email senior meta-reviewer' links on CMT to send emails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary and contributions (review field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper motivation, key contributions and achievements in a paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section helps ACs and can reveal misunderstandings; include theoretical, methodological, algorithmic, empirical, bridging, or critical-analysis contributions. See Examples of Review Content for sample phrasings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths (review field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the strengths of the work. Typical criteria include: soundness of the claims (theoretical grounding, empirical evaluation), significance and novelty of the contribution, and relevance to the NeurIPS community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List strengths such as correctness of theoretical claims, sound empirical methodology, significance relative to prior work, expected influence on researchers/practitioners, and relevance. Cite relevant prior works precisely when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weaknesses (review field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the limitations of this work along the same axes as strengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be detailed, specific, and polite. Avoid vague subjective complaints. Do not review your level of interest—focus on the scientific contribution. Suggest concrete ways to address limitations when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness (review field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims and method correct? Is the empirical methodology correct?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify anything incorrect with the paper; incorrect claims or methodology are primary reasons for rejection. Be detailed, specific, polite, and thoroughly motivate criticisms so authors can respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (review field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper well written?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate clarity of exposition and give specific examples of parts needing revision to improve clarity. Note structural issues, notation problems, missing equation numbers, or incorrect appendix references as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to prior work (review field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it clearly discussed how this work differs from previous contributions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the submission has due scholarship and explains differences to prior literature. Related work should explain differences, not merely list prior work. Papers within two months before deadline are contemporaneous—detailed comparisons not required but encouraged for camera-ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (review field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there enough details to reproduce the major results of this work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate reproducibility; if not reproducible, list this among weaknesses. Check for missing experimental details, parameter settings, or proofs; consider supplementary material if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional feedback, suggestions, and questions (review field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Free-form space for additional comments, suggestions for improvement, and questions for authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include constructive suggestions, requests for experiments or clarifications (e.g., 'I would like to see results of experiment X' or 'Please include parameter settings for Y'). Be specific about what you want clarified in the author response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (numerical acceptance guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Score should reflect your assessment of the submission's contributions; do NOT adjust to match conference acceptance rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale and interpretations provided: 10 = Top 5% of accepted NeurIPS papers (groundbreaking); 9 = Top 15% (excellent); 8 = Top 50% (very good); 7 = good (accept); 6 = marginally above threshold; 5 = marginally below threshold; 4 = okay but not good enough (reject); 3 = clear reject; 2 = strong reject; 1 = trivial/wrong/already known. Use these descriptions when choosing a score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (self-assessed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate how certain you are about your assessment on a 1–5 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5: absolutely certain, very familiar with related work; 4: confident but not absolute; 3: fairly confident (may have not checked math/details thoroughly); 2: willing to defend but likely unfamiliar with some central parts; 1: educated guess—not in your area or hard to understand; math/details not checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader impact adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the authors adequately addressed the broader impact of their work, including potential negative ethical and societal implications?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must include a broader impact statement discussing both positive and negative outcomes. Indicate yes, no, or only partially whether the broader impact section was adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns flag
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the submission raise potential ethical concerns (methods, applications, or data that create/reinforce unfair bias or have a primary purpose of harm)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No and briefly explain if concerns exist. This rating is independent of the review score; if AC shares concern, dedicated ethics reviewers may be assigned. Your duty is to flag papers needing further review for ethics expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior reviewing/resubmission disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you previously reviewed or area chaired (a version of) this work for another archival venue?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No. This helps ACs/SACs contextualize your review in light of resubmission statements by authors. AC may share prior-context information with reviewers if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agree to abide by NeurIPS Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must agree to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to CodeOfConduct provided. Reviews must accord with the code; avoid discriminatory comments and be professional and polite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to area chair
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the 'Confidential Comments to Area Chair' text field for remarks you wish to keep from authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit comparisons to other submissions and blunt criticisms here. If you accidentally learn author identities, do not divulge them, and you may report them confidentially to AC here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have an opportunity to respond to reviews before decisions; reviewers must read and (if appropriate) respond to each author response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ignore author responses. Update your review to indicate whether you agree or disagree with the response and be specific if your opinion remains the same (explain what the author response failed to address).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion phase engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: After author response, the AC will initiate a discussion to encourage reviewers to come to consensus; reviewers should engage actively in discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion is important for borderline submissions and those with differing reviewer assessments. Consider other reviewers' viewpoints, be open to changing your mind, but you are not required to. Consensus is valuable but not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of review content (illustrative guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide provides many examples of good review language for 'Contributions', 'Quality', 'Clarity', 'Originality', and 'Significance'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided sample quotes and OpenReview/nips30 examples as templates for phrasing strengths/weaknesses, and to clarify expectations (e.g., what counts as a contribution, how to point out technical issues with constructive detail).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer evaluation by ACs (meta-review scoring of reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs will evaluate the quality of each review using three scores: 'exceeded expectations', 'met expectations', and 'failed to meet expectations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top 8% of reviewers by these scores will be awarded free NeurIPS registrations; the top 30% will have registrations reserved for a limited time. Lowest scoring reviewers may not be invited in future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain reviewer profile for good matching (TPMS & OpenReview)
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS uses TPMS and OpenReview to assign submissions to ACs and reviewers; reviewers should log into TPMS and OpenReview to ensure profiles are up to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stale profile causes poor assignments that may be outside your expertise. Keep profile keywords and publications current to improve match quality.
